documents_expected.why: grants page: who is eligible, two-step process, what is not funded
application guide with the checklist of required parts

eligibility.rule: Public agencies, federally recognised tribes or 501(c)(3) nonprofits; others through a fiscal sponsor
alt_quotes: Public Agencies, including Joint Power Authorities and Federally-Recognized Indian Tribes
Other community-based organizations and non-federally-recognized tribes may apply with a 501(c)(3) fiscal sponsor

eligibility.rule: Consistent with the funding source and the Conservancy's enabling law
eligibility.quote: Consistent with purposes of the funding source.

eligibility.rule: CEQA documentation complete (or exempt) before the grant is authorised
eligibility.quote: Unless an exemption applies to the project or to the work being funded, such as the exemption for feasibility or planning studies, the required CEQA documentation must be complete before the Conservancy authorizes a grant.

eligibility.rule: Capacity to administer state funds, or a fiscal sponsor
eligibility.quote: Grantee capacity - The grantee has the ability to administer the funds and conduct the project in a manner that will meet the State's requirements and will protect the grantee from potential financial or legal risk.

eligibility.rule: Legal right to work on the site
eligibility.quote: Site ownership/control - The grantee has or will have the legal right to carry out the project on the land on which the project is proposed.
Long-term management - The grantee has a plan for the long-term management, maintenance, and monitoring of the project.
We do not fund operation and maintenance activities.

documents.quote: The first step in the application process is to submit a pre-application.

documents.item: Application cover sheet, description, selection criteria, tasks and schedule, cost estimate, maps and plans
documents.quote: Checklist items 1-6 are required for all applications.
Checklist item 7 is only required for non-profit applicants.
For Implementation projects, applicants must include the response (i.e. “Corps Consultation Review Document”) from the Conservation Corps consultation.

effort.quote: Most Conservancy grants are awarded through a rolling pre-application solicitation.

effort.step: If invited, email the full application
effort.quote: If the Conservancy determines the project is priority for funding, based on Eligibility and Project Selection Criteria (found here), and there is available Conservancy funding for the project, applicants will be invited to submit a full application.
alt_quotes: Submit the application by email to grants@scc.ca.gov.

notes: Most grants $200,000 to $5,000,000; no stated maximum or minimum. Leverage of non-state resources is a selection criterion, not a requirement. Support letters are asked only after a successful application. Reporting duties are in the Grantee Manual (not linked as a requirement page). The pre-application and application are Word files (read since gather-3); the application guide was cut by the 8-document bound.
